intro: Mind your head as you go down. You are entering Özkonak Underground City, a rock settlement in Nevşehir province, dating from the 4th century AD. It lies north of Avanos, and it hides a defensive arrangement unique in Cappadocia: pipes cut between the storeys so that hot oil could be poured on attackers.
history: How was this place found? In 1972 a farmer watering his field north of Avanos noticed the water disappearing into the ground. Below lay this underground city. Four of its levels are open today. What sets it apart from Cappadocia's other underground cities are the narrow pipes cut between the storeys: while attackers struggled at the rolling stone door, hot liquid could be poured down on them.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the rolling stone doors and the defensive pipes, then the ventilation shafts and the wine presses and stores.
facts: Did you know? The ventilation shafts were calculated to carry fresh air to rooms ten storeys down, and they still work today. The underground city was found in 1972 by a farmer who noticed his irrigation water disappearing. And those pipes cut between the storeys let hot liquid be poured on attackers — a defensive arrangement unique in Cappadocia.
outro: This brings our tour of Özkonak Underground City to an end. Before you go, please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Thank you for exploring with us, and enjoy your visit.
